en.name: Rice vermicelli, dried
en.summary: Dried rice vermicelli is shelf-stable purely because it has been dried. A sealed bag keeps about 2 years from purchase and about 1 year once opened. Both figures are borrowed from dry pasta — no Taiwanese, Japanese or Hong Kong authority publishes a home shelf life for dried 米粉 — and once the noodles are soaked or cooked, an entirely different and much shorter set of rules applies.
en.pantry: Keep the sealed bag in a dry, ventilated cupboard away from the stove, where it runs about 2 years from purchase; reseal tightly once opened and use it within about 1 year. Nothing else is preserving these noodles — there is no salt, no acid and no oil doing any work, only the absence of water — so humidity is the whole story. The strands are brittle and hygroscopic, and a bundle that has taken up damp will mould from the inside out where you cannot see it.
en.fridge: Dried rice vermicelli should not be refrigerated; a fridge is humid and the noodles are a dry good. The fridge is for the same noodles after soaking or cooking, when they become a wet rice product: cool them quickly, keep them covered at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and never leave a bowl of soaked noodles standing warm on the counter. Wet rice products are among the foods where holding them warm is the actual hazard, not a technicality.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is given for dried rice vermicelli, and it needs none — a couple of years in a dry cupboard is more than any household gets through. Freezing the dry bundles only risks condensation each time the bag comes in and out. Cooked rice vermicelli freezes badly: the strands break and go pasty on thawing, so cook what you will eat.
spoilage: Strands gone soft or bendy rather than brittle and snapping cleanly.
A musty or sour smell when the bag is opened.
Mould in the heart of a bundle, which is where it starts.
Webbing, small moths or fine dust in a long-opened bag.
tips: Decant into an airtight jar or clip the bag properly; damp is the only real threat.
Store well away from the rice cooker, the kettle and the sink.
Soak only what you will cook, and refrigerate any soaked surplus at once.
Snap a strand to test it — good vermicelli breaks cleanly rather than bending.

faq.q: How long does dried rice vermicelli keep?
faq.a: About 2 years from purchase in a sealed bag, and about 1 year once opened. Both figures are borrowed from dry pasta.

faq.q: Does dried 米粉 need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: No — it is a dry good and a fridge is humid. Only soaked or cooked noodles go in the fridge.

faq.q: How do you know dried rice vermicelli has gone off?
faq.a: It bends instead of snapping, smells musty, or has mould in the middle of the bundle. All three mean it took up moisture.

zh.name: 米粉（乾）
zh.summary: 乾燥米粉之所以能常溫保存，完全只因為它被乾燥過。未開封的袋裝從購買日起算約 2 年，開封後約 1 年。這兩個數字都借自乾燥義大利麵——台灣、日本、香港都沒有機關公布過乾米粉的家庭保存期限——而且一旦泡開或煮過，適用的就是另一套短得多的規則。
zh.pantry: 未開封的袋子放在乾燥通風、遠離爐火的櫥櫃，從購買日起算約 2 年；開封後確實封緊，約 1 年內用完。沒有別的東西在保存這些麵——沒有鹽、沒有酸、也沒有油在做事，只有「沒有水」這一件事——所以濕度就是全部的重點。米粉脆而吸濕，受潮的麵束會從你看不到的內部開始發霉。
zh.fridge: 乾米粉不該冷藏；冰箱潮濕，而它是乾貨。冰箱是留給泡開或煮過之後的米粉的，那時它已經變成含水的米製品：請快速降溫、加蓋放 4 °C 以下，絕對不要讓一碗泡好的米粉溫溫地放在檯面上。濕的米製品正是那種「放著微溫」本身就是危害的食物，不是形式上的講究。
zh.freezer: 乾米粉沒有給冷凍期限，也不需要——乾燥櫥櫃裡的兩年，已經超過任何家庭的消耗速度。把乾麵束冷凍只會在每次進出時多一次結露風險。煮過的米粉也不適合冷凍：解凍後會斷、會糊，所以要煮多少吃多少。
spoilage: 麵條變軟、可以彎折，而不是脆得一折就斷。
拆袋時聞到霉味或酸味。
麵束中心發霉——那正是它開始的地方。
開封很久的袋子裡出現絲網、小蛾或細粉屑。
tips: 倒進密封罐，或把袋口確實夾好；受潮是唯一真正的威脅。
遠離電鍋、熱水瓶和水槽。
要煮多少泡多少，泡多的立刻冷藏。
折一根測試看看——好的米粉會乾脆地斷，而不是彎曲。

faq.a: 未開封從購買日起算約 2 年，開封後約 1 年。兩個數字都借自乾燥義大利麵。
不需要，它是乾貨，而冰箱很潮濕。只有泡開或煮過的才要冷藏。
折起來會彎不會斷、聞起來有霉味，或麵束中心長霉。這三種都代表它已經受潮。
